title: A fake invoice email takes over the doctor's email

steps.situation: An email arrives: "URGENT: unpaid invoice. Click here to view and pay today." It looks like it is from a supplier, but the sender's address has a spelling mistake.

owner.text: Click the link to see what the invoice is
owner.feedback: That link is how they get in. Never open a link in a surprise "urgent" email.

owner.text: Don't click. Leave the email where it is and ask IT to look at it
owner.feedback: Right. Not clicking stops it here, and IT can warn everyone else.

owner.text: Delete the email so nobody else clicks it
owner.feedback: Deleting it loses the evidence IT needs. Leave it and tell IT.

staff.text: Open it to check whether it is for us
staff.feedback: Opening the link is exactly what the sender wants. Don't click anything in it.

staff.text: Don't click. Tell Dr. Rao the same email came to you
staff.feedback: Right. If it came to you too, it is aimed at the whole clinic.

staff.text: Forward it to Dr. Rao so he can decide
staff.feedback: Forwarding passes the dangerous link on. Just tell him it came in.

steps.situation: Too late: earlier this morning Dr. Rao clicked the link and typed his email password into a page that looked like his email login. Now his password doesn't work.

owner.text: Change the password on the same computer, right now
owner.feedback: That computer may be watched now. Change the password from a different phone or computer.

owner.text: Change the email password from a different phone or computer, then call IT
owner.feedback: Right. A new password, typed somewhere safe, locks them out.

owner.text: Wait and see if anything strange happens
owner.feedback: Whoever has the password can read and send email as you right now. Act now.

staff.text: Stop using the doctor's computer and call the saved IT contact
staff.feedback: Right. Keep off that computer and get IT on the phone.

staff.text: Try to log in to the doctor's email for him
staff.feedback: Never type the doctor's password anywhere. Leave the account to him and IT.

steps.situation: Patients start calling. They got a message "from the clinic" asking them to pay a pending lab fee online.

front_desk.text: Tell callers the message is fake, they must not pay, and write down who called
front_desk.feedback: Right. A clear "it's fake, don't pay" protects patients, and your list helps the report.

front_desk.text: Give them the clinic's own bank details so they can pay properly
front_desk.feedback: There is no lab fee. Tell them not to pay anything.

front_desk.text: Say you don't know anything about it
front_desk.feedback: Patients trust the clinic. Tell them clearly it's fake and not to pay.

billing.text: Refund anyone who says they paid, from the clinic's account
billing.feedback: The money went to the scammer, not the clinic. Note their names; Dr. Rao decides about refunds.

billing.text: Write down every patient who says they paid, and tell them to call 1930 now
billing.feedback: Right. 1930 is the national cyber-fraud helpline. The sooner they call, the better the chance of getting the money back.

billing.text: Ignore it: billing didn't send that message
billing.feedback: Patients are losing money in the clinic's name. Help them act fast.

owner.text: Ask IT to check the email account for anything the attacker changed, and to turn on login codes sent to your phone
owner.feedback: Right. Attackers often leave a setting that copies your email to them. IT can find it and remove it.

owner.text: Open a new email address and keep using the old one too
owner.feedback: The old account stays in the attacker's hands until IT has checked it.

steps.situation: Patients' names and phone numbers in the doctor's email were seen by the attacker.

owner.text: No need to report: the clinic itself lost no money
owner.feedback: Patient details were exposed. That is a personal-data breach under the DPDP Act, even with no money lost.

owner.text: Report to CERT-In within 6 hours and start the patient-data breach record
owner.feedback: Right. Report now; the breach record covers the patients whose details were seen.

owner.text: Post an apology on social media and leave it there
owner.feedback: Telling patients is good, but the formal reports come first: CERT-In within 6 hours.

staff.text: Write down what you saw and when, and give it to Dr. Rao
staff.feedback: Right. Your notes become the incident timeline.

staff.text: Clear the call list so it doesn't worry anyone
staff.feedback: That list is evidence. Keep it and write down what you saw.
